result.summary: 0 exact, 6 behavioral, 0 stub parts. Logic is ok; approximate or missing: timing, analog, power. Check the 13 items in testOnRealDevice on hardware before trusting it.

notes: arduino-uno: Cycle-counted at 16 MHz on a deterministic virtual clock, so delay()/millis() are exact in virtual time. Peripherals the emulator lacks (e.g. some timer modes, sleep) and the crystal's ±50 ppm drift are not modelled.

ssd1306-oled-i2c: Bytes take real I2C time (set by the MCU's TWI clock), but the panel shows a new frame instantly: no refresh rate, no tearing, and the clock/pre-charge settings (0xD5, 0xD9, 0xDB) have no effect.
pushbutton: Switches instantly; real contacts bounce for 1–10 ms, which firmware must debounce.
buzzer: Starts and stops instantly; the internal ~2.3 kHz oscillator is not simulated cycle by cycle and there is no audio output yet.

arduino-uno: Pins are ideal sources with 25 Ω output resistance. Digital inputs use the datasheet thresholds (low ≤ 0.3·VCC, high ≥ 0.6·VCC) and keep their last level in between. The ADC reads the solved net voltage against a 5 V reference; AREF, noise and input capacitance are ignored.
ssd1306-oled-i2c: Contrast is shown as a simple brightness scale. No OLED burn-in, no brightness difference between few and many lit pixels.
pushbutton: Closed contact is 0.01 Ω, open contact is a perfect open circuit.
buzzer: Modelled as a 180 Ω load (≈ 25 mA at 5 V) with a reverse-blocking diode; loudness ramps linearly from 3 V to 5 V.
arduino-uno: 5 V / 3.3 V rails are stiff sources. Per-pin current above 40 mA is flagged; total-package (200 mA) and regulator limits, VIN and brownout are not simulated.
ssd1306-oled-i2c: Draws a fixed 10 mA from VCC (real modules use about 8 to 25 mA depending on how many pixels are lit) and only works between 2.8 and 5.5 V. 4.7 kOhm pull-ups on SDA and SCL to VCC.
buzzer: Current draw is realistic for a 5 V active buzzer, so GPIO overcurrent checks apply.

testOnRealDevice: uno (arduino-uno): Total current from many pins (200 mA package limit)
uno (arduino-uno): Anything powered from VIN or the 3.3 V pin (50 mA max)
uno (arduino-uno): Analog readings near the input thresholds
uno (arduino-uno): Upload through the bootloader (arduino-cli upload)
oled1 (ssd1306-oled-i2c): Which address your module really uses (check the jumper on the back; some are labelled 0x78/0x7A, which is 0x3C/0x3D shifted left)
oled1 (ssd1306-oled-i2c): Readability of the contrast setting in daylight
oled1 (ssd1306-oled-i2c): Supply current if you run from a battery
bz1 (buzzer): Driving with tone() or PWM (active buzzers can sound distorted)
Unplug each module while running to see how the firmware copes (or rehearse with inject_fault disconnect / i2c_nack).
global: Time is virtual and deterministic: real oscillators drift and real sensors are noisy (use inject_fault noisy to rehearse).
All grounds are one node and wires have no resistance or inductance; long wires, motor noise and ground bounce are not modelled.
Supply rails are ideal: brownouts when motors start are not simulated; measure the real supply under load.
